items.pattern: subject does the action itself (She dyed her boots) instead of have/get + object + participle
items.sk: „{wrong}“ znamená, že to podmet robí sám. Treba Causative: „{right}“.
items.cz: „{wrong}“ znamená, že to podmět dělá sám. Je potřeba Causative: „{right}“.
items.en: “{wrong}” means the subject did it. Use the Causative: “{right}”.

items.pattern: object + was/were + participle (Her boots were dyed)
items.en: Practise the Causative here: “{right}”.

items.pattern: have/get + object + base form
items.sk: V Causative patrí za predmet past participle: „{right}“.
items.cz: V Causative následuje po předmětu past participle: „{right}“.
items.en: In the Causative the object is followed by a past participle: “{right}”.

items.pattern: have/get + object + Past Simple form (got it took)
items.sk: Za predmet patrí past participle, nie Past Simple: „{right}“.
items.cz: Po předmětu patří past participle, ne Past Simple: „{right}“.
items.en: After the object use the past participle, not Past Simple: “{right}”.

items.pattern: irregular verb with a regular -ed participle
items.sk: Nepravidelné sloveso: past participle je „{right}“, nie „{wrong}“.
items.cz: Nepravidelné sloveso: past participle je „{right}“, ne „{wrong}“.
items.en: Irregular verb: the past participle is “{right}”, not “{wrong}”.

items.pattern: have/get + participle + object (got checked her slides)
items.en: The order is “have/get + thing + past participle”: “{right}”.

items.pattern: had + participle + object (had dyed her boots)
items.sk: Toto je Past Perfect. Causative má poradie „had + vec + past participle“: „{right}“.
items.cz: Toto je Past Perfect. Causative má pořadí „had + věc + past participle“: „{right}“.
items.en: That is Past Perfect. The Causative order is “had + thing + participle”: “{right}”.

items.pattern: have + object + to + verb (had the kitchen to film)
items.en: The Causative has no “to”: “{right}”.

items.pattern: have + person + to + verb
items.en: After “have + person” use the verb without “to”: “{right}”.

items.pattern: get + person + base form without to
items.en: After “get + person” use “to” + verb: “{right}”.

items.pattern: gave + object + to + verb for 'dať urobiť'
items.en: Do not use “give” here; use the Causative: “{right}”.

items.pattern: let + object + verb for 'nechať si urobiť'
items.en: “let” means “allow”; for a service use the Causative: “{right}”.

items.pattern: made + object + participle
items.en: “make” means force; a service is “have/get”: “{right}”.

items.pattern: extra reflexive pronoun (had herself her hair cut) from 'dala si'
items.en: The reflexive is not translated: “{right}”.

items.pattern: has/gets for a past event (last summer, the night before)
items.en: The event was in the past: “{right}”, not “{wrong}”.

items.pattern: has had + object + participle with a finished past time
items.sk: S minulým časovým údajom patrí Past Simple: „{right}“.
items.cz: S minulým časovým údajem patří Past Simple: „{right}“.
items.en: A finished past time takes Past Simple: “{right}”.

items.pattern: from/of instead of by before the person who does it
items.en: The person who does it is introduced by “by”: “{right}”, not “{wrong}”.

items.pattern: preposition added before the colour (dyed on purple)
items.en: No preposition before the colour: “{right}”.

items.pattern: her/his/their dropped before the object or agent
items.en: The possessive is missing: “{right}”.

items.pattern: until instead of while for 'kým' (= during)
items.sk: „Kým“ tu znamená „počas“, teda „while“; „until“ je „až dovtedy, kým“.
items.en: Here it means “during”, so “while”; “until” means “up to the time”.
